cause: The quick gate backend fallback could not start macOS sandbox-exec and reported: sandbox-exec: sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted.
impact: The sandboxed quick gate is not a host acceptance signal in this environment; the required host full gate was run separately.
lesson: Keep sandbox capability failures separate from product failures and use the host full gate for release-grade evidence.

cause: The first host full gate reported three failures: the legacy graph smoke timed out after 5 seconds while importing plotting dependencies; cs_did failed with 422: model.genesis cs_did does not accept did_cohort_col, did_mode; sa_did failed with the analogous rejection.

evidence.ref: host full gate output before targeted fixes

impact: The gate could not be accepted until startup dependency loading and native DID family parameter projection were corrected.
lesson: A green focused suite is insufficient when the host gate still exposes startup and family-contract integration regressions.

cause: After the startup import isolation and native family projection fixes, the host full gate completed successfully.
lesson: Only claim the integrated gate after backend, invariants, frontend, and typecheck stages all finish with their explicit results.

cause: A live P7 Hurdle negative-binomial execution returned a typed failed result, but the generic workflow executor previously committed it as completed.
impact: A non-convergent analysis could have been reported as successful and persisted a misleading analysis artifact.
lesson: Typed non-completed results must fail closed before artifact persistence.

cause: After the fail-closed guard, the same Hurdle negative-binomial browser execution rendered execution failed, workflow failed, zero post-estimation artifacts, and no committed P7 artifact.
impact: The runtime now exposes non-convergence as a visible failure instead of silently degrading to success.
lesson: Live acceptance must verify both failure visibility and the absence of committed result artifacts.

cause: Historical Report browser acceptance exposed duplicate figure marker coef_plot and a retry exposed LLM_UPSTREAM_ERROR: ReadError; the first complete report was withheld until a later retry succeeded.
impact: The upstream retry remains an external reliability concern; it did not get converted into a false report success.
lesson: Transient upstream errors and duplicate markers must remain visible until a complete accepted report is independently observed.

cause: A later manually reviewed Report browser run saved an exportable report with 314 provenance facts, 15 inventoried figures, no duplicate figure marker, and no upstream ReadError.
impact: The Report consumer/provider chain has one complete successful browser acceptance after the earlier failures.
lesson: Report completion requires saved, exportable, provenance-backed state, not only a successful upstream request.

cause: A fresh Notebook browser execution completed with output contract passed and no ARTIFACT_UNDECLARED diagnostics after the projection was aligned with the declared artifact contract.
impact: Notebook real-chain acceptance no longer carries the previously observed undeclared-artifact warning for the verified paths.
lesson: Artifact manifests must project the declared contract scope and reject ambient leakage without hiding it.

cause: Synthetic Control first rejected an incompatible long-table period shape and a six-row fixture was blocked by the configured modeling minimum; a corrected 30-period wide fixture then completed through the browser with a durable typed result.
impact: The shape and sample guards remained visible, while the valid Synthetic Control consumer/provider chain completed without a silent fallback.
lesson: Real acceptance fixtures must match operation geometry and pass the same sample guards as production data.

cause: The P7 registry contains 64 operations; 14 unique operations were attempted in manually reviewed browser chains, 13 completed successfully, and one intentionally failed closed for non-convergence.
lesson: Generic workflow coverage is not equivalent to individually reviewed browser acceptance; preserve the remaining operation matrix as an explicit gap.

cause: The host full gate completed after the live-chain fixes and stopped with an accepted result.
lesson: Release claims require the host gate's final exit status across backend, golden, frontend, and typecheck stages.

cause: The first final host gate reported five failures: four memory fixtures became review_due after their hard-coded review date passed, and one graph projection assertion omitted the newly required immutable upload workflow source.
lesson: Calendar-sensitive fixtures must derive a future review boundary, and source projection tests must include the immutable workflow source without weakening runtime provenance.

cause: The linear requirement to click all 64 P7 operations was replaced by registry-derived execution for every operation, one real browser execution for each of 18 declared families, and separate ordinary-language, Report, and Hurdle boundary chains.
lesson: Scale acceptance by deriving the full denominator from declarations and reserve expensive browser and provider work for family and cross-layer boundaries.

cause: Final review found that declared family contract lookup or builder projection errors could be converted into an empty Genesis editor schema and continue silently.
impact: Declared family lookup and wire-projection failures now remain visible and fail closed instead of presenting an incomplete editor as usable.
lesson: A declaration-driven editor must distinguish an undeclared capability from a broken declared contract and never map the latter to an empty schema.

cause: The local acceptance runner coordinates immutable admissions and durable results but does not cryptographically prove that a browser observation or completion record was produced by an independent witness.
impact: Runner ledgers are operational coordination evidence, not a sole tamper-resistant witness; final browser claims rely on independently observed live sessions in addition to the runner.
lesson: Do not promote a local QA coordinator into a cryptographic browser witness without a separate signed observer architecture and explicit production-neutral hooks.

cause: The final stable-code host gate completed successfully after the fail-closed Genesis review changes.
lesson: The final gate must run after the last production behavior change and on an unchanged worktree hash.

cause: The P7 Agent, upload-only Notebook, Report, persistent panel, batch acceptance, failure visibility, and integrated gate objectives reached their declared verification boundaries.
impact: The development line is ready for a local checkpoint commit with the accepted QA witness trust boundary remaining explicit.
lesson: Completion separates operation-wide automation, family browser acceptance, true provider chains, full repository gates, and explicitly accepted proof boundaries.
